Cati Bestard

“Cati Bestard’s conceptual photographic installations and sculptures are evidence of a deep and open-ended inquiry into how photography interacts with the built environment.”

– Adama Delphine Fawundu & Klea McKenna (2022 Jury).

blocks.alt: Image © Cati Bestard. Courtesy of the artist.

blocks.text: […] The project began with black and white large-format images of the corners of my home. At the time, I was thinking, in a queer sense, about what happens when you move away from the center and focus on something that is normally unseen... Interrogating systems and social constructs to reflect around the way we experience life and care for the world, are the underlying motivations of my image making, always starting from my everyday life surroundings and experiences. […]

blocks.html:
Cati Bestard was born in Mallorca (Spain). She received her MFA from Columbia University in 2018. Her work has been exhibited at Ulterior Gallery, Times Square Space, Jewish Museum, Ortega y Gasset Projects, Museu Palau Soterra, Crush Curatorial and Untitled Miami. She has been a resident at the Institute of Investigative Living with Andrea Zittel (Joshua Tree, 2017), Hercules Art Studio Program (New York, 2018-2020), and Art Workspace Easthampton (Easthampton, 2021). She co-directs Dilalica, an exhibition space based in Barcelona. She has taught in the photography department at Columbia University, and currently teaches at Smith and Amherst Colleges.
